answer: Memory-hard admission puzzle: each new identity must solve a 256 MB Argon2 puzzle taking about 20 seconds, and the solution is bound to its public key. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 puzzles and 256 GB of RAM time, so attacker cost scales linearly with identities. Reaching the summit of rewards stays costly; a whisper of spare hardware cannot fake it, and a verifier checks each proof in one pulse of milliseconds.
